name: Anna Ancher
bio: Anna Ancher was a Danish artist associated with the Skagen Painters, an artist colony on the northern point of Jylland, Denmark. She is considered one of Denmark's greatest visual artists.

paintings.title: Sunlight in the Blue Room
paintings.story: Sunlight in the Blue Room is an 1891 painting by Anna Ancher, an innovative Danish painter who was a central figure with the Skagen Painters. With its many shades of blue and the sunlight pouring through the window, the painting is one of her most prominent works.
facts: Inspired by the works of the artists who spent their summers at the inn, she decided to take up painting as a profession at a time when women were not admitted to the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts.

The Skagen Painters were a close-knit group of mainly Danish artists who gathered each summer from the late 1870s in the fishing village of Skagen in the far north of Jutland, painting the local fishermen and their own gatherings and celebrations.

paintings.title: The Artist's Mother Ane Hedvig Brøndum in the Red Room
paintings.story: The artist's mother Ane Hedvig Brøndum in the red room is an oil on canvas painting by Danish painter Anna Ancher from 1909. It is held at the National Gallery of Denmark, in Copenhagen.
facts: Anna Ancher made several paintings of her mother, Anna Hedvig (Ane) Brøndum (1826-1916), who was married to merchant and innkeeper Erik Andersen Brøndum (1820–90).
After her husband's death in 1890 she ran Brøndum's Hotel, with her son Degn Brøndum, until she was 70 years old.

paintings.title: Harvesters (Ancher)
paintings.story: Harvesters is a 1905 oil painting on canvas by the Danish artist Anna Ancher, a member of the artists' community known as the Skagen Painters which flourished in Skagen in the north of Jutland in Denmark in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
facts: Vincent van Gogh exhibited a harvest scene at Den Frie in Copenhagen in 1893; though there is no record of Ancher having seen the exhibition, a letter to Martha Johansen reveals she was aware of it and the trend towards Symbolism that some of the works by Van Gogh and Gauguin exhibited there displayed.

paintings.title: Stine Bollerhus counts the money earned selling bread. Repeat.
paintings.story: From the auction notes: Anna Ancher has painted the motif twice. The Art Museums of Skagen have a version from 1879, which is signed Anna Brøndum (Inv. No. 1632). The present painting is signed Anna Ancher and must therefore have been painted after 18 August 1880, when Anna and Michael Ancher were married. Stine and her husband Per Bollerhus were Skagen locals and some of the town's eccentrics. They lived in Østerby and made a living by bringing out bread from Saxild's bakery. Stine and Per Bollerhus often appear in the Skagen painters' works, and Anna Ancher has painted Stine several times. See "Other versions".

paintings.title: An old woman in her kitchen.
paintings.story: From the auction notes: Stine Bollerhus feeding chickens. Anna Ancher's maiden name was Brøndum. The present painting was done in the years just before she married Michael Ancher. Exhibited: Dansk Kunsthandel, “Maleriudstilling”, Industriudstillingsbygningen 1879 no. 17. This was the first time Anna Brøndum participated in a major public art exhibition. The painting is mentioned three times in Elisabeth Fabritius, “Anna og Michael Ancher. Breve og fotografier”, 2018, Vol. 1. In letter 207 dated 11.6.1879, Michael Ancher writes to Anna about the exhibiton organized by Dansk Kunsthandel (in Danish): “You probably have to pay 3 or 4 kroner if you want to have Stine in the kitchen with you at his exhibition in the industrial building”. In letter 232 dated 16.8.1879 Anna's cousin Martha Møller writes to her about Dansk Kunsthandel's exhibition (in Danish): “Dearest Anna, it is also really enjoyable to see your painting up there; - it is much, much better in colour than the one with the woman counting the money”. In letter 234 dated 17.8.1879 Thora Lunddahl writes to Anna about Dansk Kunsthandel's exhibition (in Danish): “On the other hand, I am looking forward to the exhibition and hope that its painting section will be extended over time, which seems to me to be very short. I have read with pleasure about Ancher's painting, which I hope I will have the opportunity to see. It's true, I can greet you from Stine (who feeds chickens). Ms Kinch and I ventured one day into the premises in Hovedvagts or ny Østergade, whatever it's called, to take a look at it”.

paintings.title: A young woman from Skagen with a black headscarf.
Communion in Skagen Church. Study.
paintings.story: From the auction notes: The present painting is a study for “Altergang i Skagen kirke” (Communion in Skagen Church), which Anna Ancher painted two versions of in 1899. Both are today at The Art Museums of Skagen. One, which was exhibited at Charlottenborg 1930 no. 23. (Inv. No. 1073); the other at Charlottenborg 1900 as no. 5, and that one was purchased at Bruun Rasmussen auction 915, 2023 no. 135 for a hammer price of DKK 550,000. In the present painting, the priest is seen during communion on the left side, while in the two finished paintings Anna Ancher has omitted this and instead focused on the churchgoers. See "Other versions".

paintings.title: Evening interior.
paintings.story: From the auction notes: An evening party in Brøndum's painting hall with Helga Ancher (1883–1964) in the centre performing accompanied by naval officer, later naval captain Eigil Riis-Carstensen (1892–1953). Around her from the left: Town treasurer Johan Frederik (Hansi) Brodersen (1858–1943), Degn Brøndum (1856–1932) sitting and smoking a cigar, in the back to the right Hulda Brøndum (1853–1935). In the front to the left Henny Brodersen (1868–1960) in a green dress and Marie Brøndum (1851–1945) in a violet dress. The gentleman in the wicker chair with his back turned is Inspector of dunes and Planter in Hjørring county C.F. Dahlerup (1857–1945).
